cells.tense: Right now the direction is settled, and you are living from it without argument.
cells.ask: Let one steadying thing lean on you this week. Something you keep level for someone, or an arrangement you keep true — let it take a little of your weight instead of the whole exchange running one way.
cells.core:
You have a direction and you do not argue for it. It sits in you quietly, and the rest gets kept level around it — you feel when the room needs more of something and when it needs less, and you adjust without making a fuss. That adjustment is running right now, in a dozen small moves nobody notices, and it is why things around you stay on an even keel instead of tipping.
What is rarer is being held by it. An even keel usually goes one way: you keep the balance, the balance does not keep you. Nothing is at stake in trying the other direction, and it is the thing that would make this last.
cells.sheetLine: Keeping things level and steering are the same act.
cells.verb: Choosing the direction to steer by

cells.tense: You are already bracing for a crossing you cannot write in yet.
cells.ask: Name the direction you have settled on and make one small motion toward it this week. A phone call, a note, a first step. Leave the rest unsorted for now.
cells.core:
You have picked the direction. The trouble is that you are living at the far end of the course — checking the next turn, the one after that, the way you will hold it all together when the ground moves. The planning has gone past what planning is for.
A direction does not need every corner mapped to be trustworthy. The steadying you are good at works when it can feel the ground under the actual moment, and you are standing in advance of it. The course is set. What is still being written is the walking of it, and that happens here, not ahead.

cells.tense: Some part of you is still standing where the decision happened, and the standing is what remains.
cells.ask: Keep one small thing you tend for its own sake — a plant, a person, a walk on the same day each week — and note what comes back from it. No new ambition, just the same care running forward.
cells.core:
The decision already happened, but the life that was supposed to start from it is thin on the ground. You know the direction, or you knew it, and somewhere the walking of it stopped. What is left is the sense of a decision that did not come to much — and a person still braced inside a room the decision has already left.
This does not need a bigger decision. It needs the smaller tending that happens after one — the daily keeping of a thing that grows when you are steady with it. That kind of care does not exhaust, and it can carry a direction without asking you to decide it over every morning.

cells.tense: The writing is already happening in this room, and no one has put their name on it.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you arrange for other people and say, once, in plain words, that you chose it. One sentence, to yourself or to someone there.
cells.core:
You are already steering. A good run of this looks like small corrections made early and without comment — a call made before it is owed, a move when the room tilts, a thing set right before anyone has to ask. The direction holds, and nothing needs announcing for it to hold.
What is happening now is the same steering, running without a claim. You file it under circumstances, or under what needed doing, and the work keeps going exactly as well. Naming it changes nothing about the work. It changes who gets to have done it — which matters when the next call comes and the direction has to come from somewhere you recognize.

The sentence that served the writer more than the person was the one that made the whole life sound stalled — cut.
